source_note: Compiled from dermatologist-reviewed content (CeraVe Skin Smarts, reviewed by Dr. Nkem Ugonabo, MD) and American Academy of Dermatology guidance. Paraphrased and restructured for internal knowledge base use.

skin_types.name: Oily Skin
characteristics: Shiny or greasy appearance, especially in the T-zone (forehead, nose, chin)
Enlarged, more visible pores
Prone to blackheads and acne blemishes
Skin often feels heavier or thicker to the touch
skin_types.possible_upside: May show fewer visible fine lines/wrinkles over time due to natural oil content, per AAD.
skin_types.home_test_watch_and_wait: Skin appears shiny all over the face after cleansing and 30 minutes of no product.
skin_types.home_test_blotting_sheet: Blotting sheets pick up significant oil from all areas of the face.

care_tips.cleanser: Oil-free, non-comedogenic foaming cleanser to remove excess surface oil without stripping the barrier.
care_tips.moisturizer: Still required daily; choose oil-free, non-comedogenic, gel-based formulas rather than heavy creams.

skin_types.name: Dry Skin
characteristics: Skin feels tight, especially after washing
Visible flaking, roughness, or scaliness
Dull or dehydrated appearance
More visible fine lines
Can be itchy or irritated
causes: Compromised skin barrier (reduced ability to retain water)
skin_types.home_test_watch_and_wait: Skin feels flaky, rough, or tight 30 minutes after cleansing.
skin_types.home_test_blotting_sheet: Blotting sheets absorb little to no oil from any area.

care_tips.cleanser: Gentle, fragrance-free, hydrating cleanser (cream or oil-based cleansing formulas work well).
care_tips.moisturizer: Thicker, cream-based (not lotion) formulas applied immediately after cleansing to lock in moisture.

skin_types.name: Combination Skin
characteristics: Oily T-zone (forehead, nose, chin)
Drier cheeks
Presentation varies widely between individuals
May show shine in oily areas and redness/patchiness or ashy/grayish tone in drier areas (more visible on deeper skin tones)
Can shift with seasons, stress, or hormones
causes: Uneven sebaceous gland activity across facial zones
skin_types.home_test_watch_and_wait: Shine appears only around the T-zone; cheeks may feel normal to dry.
skin_types.home_test_blotting_sheet: Sheets pick up oil mainly from the T-zone only.

care_tips.approach: Zone-specific care rather than one product for the whole face.
care_tips.extra_tip: Blotting papers can be used on the T-zone during the day to manage shine.

skin_types.name: Normal Skin
characteristics: Skin feels hydrated and comfortable
Not notably oily or dry in any area
Smoother texture with less visible pores
Generally not prone to a specific recurring concern
Lower tendency toward sensitivity
skin_types.home_test_watch_and_wait: Skin feels hydrated, not dry or oily anywhere, 30 minutes after cleansing.
skin_types.home_test_blotting_sheet: Minimal oil picked up from all areas.

care_tips.moisturizer: Still necessary daily; formulas with ceramides and hyaluronic acid help maintain barrier and hydration.
care_tips.note: Can still be prone to acne regardless of skin type; non-comedogenic products still recommended.

skin_types.name: Sensitive Skin
characteristics: Can co-occur with any of the other four skin types
Reacts more easily to products or environmental triggers
May show redness, stinging, burning, or irritation after product use
causes: Compromised skin barrier (suspected, per current research)
Exposure to irritants such as fragrance
Exact cause not yet fully established medically

care_tips.general: Best evaluated with a board-certified dermatologist to identify specific triggers.
care_tips.recommended_approach: Gentle, fragrance-free routine with minimal, well-tolerated ingredients.

steps: Wash face with a gentle cleanser
Press blotting sheets to different facial zones
Hold sheets to light and compare oil absorbed per zone
